title: Participial Nouns (Third Declension)
description: Inflect nouns built like the participle, such as כֹּהֵן.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.html: A third family of nouns is built like the participle, ending in -ē with an unchangeable vowel before it: כֹּהֵן (priest), אֹיֵב (enemy), שֹׁפֵט (judge). Many nouns with a prefixed מ belong here too: מִשְׁפָּט (judgment), מַלְאָךְ (messenger).

blocks.caption: The participial nouns
blocks.html: A third family ends in -ē with an unchangeable vowel before it: כֹּהֵן (priest), אֹיֵב (enemy), שֹׁפֵט (judge). These follow the verb's law of inflection: with a vocalic suffix the tone-vowel reduces to shewa (כֹּהֲנֵי, priests of), and with a consonantal suffix it shortens. Many words formed with a prefixed m — מִשְׁפָּט (judgment), מַלְאָךְ (messenger) — belong to this family.

blocks.caption: Common confusion
blocks.html: Do not parse every word of this shape as a verb. A participle can be a verb ("keeping") or a noun ("keeper"); a word like כֹּהֵן is only a noun, but it inflects the same way.
